content.title: Isaiah 58-66 Part 1 • Dr. Ross D. Baron • Oct. 3 - 9
content.summary: Hosts Hank Smith and John Bytheway sit down with Dr. Ross D. Baron, who draws on his background living in Israel to explore the many names and titles for Jesus Christ in Isaiah. The episode emphasizes how Isaiah brings hope and ties the blessings of fasting to the reality of the Savior's redemption, with a Part 2 episode continuing the 'kinsman redeemer' theme the same day.
content.hosts_or_guests: Hosts: Hank Smith, John Bytheway; Guest: Dr. Ross D. Baron

content.title: Isaiah 58 - 66
content.summary: David Butler and Emily Belle Freeman frame Isaiah 58-66 around themes of rebellion, remembering, and recentering. Their discussion highlights the pattern of 'A Call for Help,' identifying personal needs, and being 'Covered and Claimed' by the Savior's redemption, tying Isaiah's imagery to everyday discipleship.

content.title: Isaiah 58-66: "Beauty for Ashes"
content.summary: Jared Halverson delivers an exceptionally deep, verse-by-verse dive into Isaiah 58-66, covering niche imagery like 'hatching eggs of iniquity,' 'groping for the wall,' and the 'armor of God,' alongside major themes of beauty for ashes, robes of righteousness, and the new heavens and new earth. At over three hours, it's one of the most exhaustive single-episode treatments of this block available.

content.title: Isaiah 58-66, Part 1 | Come Follow Me Insights with Taylor and Tyler
content.summary: Taylor Halverson and Tyler Griffin are joined by guest Lori Newbold for a two-part series closing out the book of Isaiah. This first installment digs into covenant-keeping, the true purpose of fasting, and the sanctity of the Sabbath as taught in Isaiah 58-66, continued in a Part 2 episode (Ep. 44, 51 min).
content.hosts_or_guests: Taylor Halverson, Tyler Griffin, with guest Lori Newbold

content.title: Ep 173 | Isaiah 58-66, Come Follow Me (October 3-9)
content.summary: Mike Day and Bryce Dunford trace the historical tension between two groups of returning exiles reflected in these chapters, then move into the messianic reading of Isaiah 61 in the Nazareth synagogue. They close with temple and wedding imagery in Isaiah 61-62 and connect Isaiah 66's imagery of Zion's travail and deliverance to Nephi's Tree of Life vision.
